mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations. This results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% despite tight labor market, indicating that the Fed will not feel compelled to hike rates aggressively.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows by more than 2% YoY, it signals a supply-side slowdown that will crimp corporate profits and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if the slowdown is accompanied by rising inventories (proxied by a widening RSAFS).
failure_condition: Supply chain pressures ease (as measured by falling shipping costs) before the industrial slowdown translates into falling profits and stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: When the Fed funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow the economy and depress S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if accompanied by a flattening yield curve (10y-2y spread narrowing).
failure_condition: The Fed pivots to a dovish stance (e.g., signaling a pause in hikes) before the restrictive policy has fully filtered through to the real economy.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts above a 1.2 million annualized rate signals overexuberant residential investment that will soon reverse, dragging down related sectors like homebuilding, lumber, and appliances. This sectoral drag will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts remain elevated for over 6 months without triggering a downturn, suggesting that the sectoral imbalances are not as severe as initially feared.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a labor market slowdown that will soon spread to the broader economy, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Other labor market indicators like jobless claims and JOLTS vacancies remain strong, suggesting that the payroll slowdown is an aberration rather than the start of a trend.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid 1% rise in the CPI over a 3-month period signals an inflation scare that will prompt the Fed to hike rates aggressively, depressing S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is especially pronounced if real GDP is already slowing, indicating that the Fed is hiking into a weakening economy.
failure_condition: The inflation spike proves transitory (e.g., driven by a one-off supply shock) and the Fed signals that it will not respond with aggressive hikes.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP growth slowing by more than 2% YoY signals a broad economic slowdown that will depress corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This slowdown signal is especially powerful if accompanied by a drop in consumer sentiment (proxied by real retail sales).
failure_condition: Leading indicators like the yield curve and stock market breadth remain bullish, suggesting that the GDP slowdown is likely to be short-lived.
